abstract: Immune evasion can arise from genetic alterations and reversible regulatory programs, but how these mechanisms jointly shape tumor states across cancers remains unclear. Here, we integrated 11 genomic and 39 bulk-derived non-genomic escape features across 10,616 tumors from The Cancer Genome Atlas to construct a pan-cancer immune escape atlas. Overall, 90% of tumors harbor at least one escape feature. Genomic escape features were linked more consistently to tumor mutational and copy-number burdens than to immune infiltration and showed clonal enrichment and evidence of positive selection. Mutations in antigen presentation machinery and mutations in the interferon γ (IFN-γ) signaling pathway were associated with attenuated immunoediting. Genomic escape subgrouping further stratified evolutionary and immunological phenotypes and outcomes in immune checkpoint blockade cohorts, whereas non-genomic subgrouping showed weaker outcome stratification. These findings position genomic escape as a coordinated evolutionary shift and provide a framework for context-specific tumor phenotyping.
